claim: Elasticity framework: output elasticity is decomposed into a probability channel and a capital channel, with a queueing multiplier only where near-capacity utilisation is evidenced.
source_title: Agent C elasticity model

figures.denominator_def: % change in annual approved new drugs per 10% improvement in the named factor

derivation: Y = N x PoS (steady state). Probability channel eps_P = 10 x ((1-PoS)/PoS) x f x theta, with PoS=0.12 [E-3002] so (1-PoS)/PoS = 7.33; f = share of attrition attributable to the factor; theta = pass-through of a 10% factor improvement into that attrition class. Capital channel eps_C = 10 x c x tau x delta, with c = share of capitalised cost the factor touches, tau = fraction of that cost responsive to the improvement, delta = marginal-program quality discount (0.4-0.8). Time-only gains are credited to output ONLY through eps_C (fixed-budget program count) because a shorter step raises the steady-state approval rate only if it frees capital or capacity; a purely parallelisable speed-up produces a one-off level shift, not a rate change.

claim: B1 target validation elasticity is estimated at 5-15% per 10% improvement, point 10%.
source_title: Agent C elasticity model

figures.unit: % change in annual approvals per 10% factor improvement
figures.denominator_def: % change in annual approved new drugs per 10% improvement in the named factor

derivation: eps_P = 10 x 7.33 x f x theta with f=0.45 (efficacy share of failures [E-3012]) and theta=0.15-0.45; = 4.9 to 14.8. Capital channel negligible. Point 9.9 rounded to 10. theta band reflects that a 10% reduction in the share of programs on non-translatable targets is not fully observable ex ante.

claim: B2 preclinical-to-clinical translation elasticity is estimated at 2-7% per 10% improvement, point 4%.
source_title: Agent C elasticity model

figures.unit: % change in annual approvals per 10% factor improvement
figures.denominator_def: % change in annual approved new drugs per 10% improvement in the named factor

derivation: eps_P = 10 x 7.33 x f x theta with f=0.25 (portion of efficacy+tox attrition attributable to model non-predictivity rather than target choice) and theta=0.10-0.35 (bounded low because zero NAMs were fully qualified under ISTAND as of Jan 2026 [E-3015]); = 1.8 to 6.4. eps_C adds ~0.3 from reduced preclinical spend (c=0.10, tau=0.30, delta=0.6). Point 4.0.

claim: B3 recruitment and site capacity elasticity is estimated at 1.5-4.0% per 10% improvement, point 2.5%.
source_title: Agent C elasticity model

figures.unit: % change in annual approvals per 10% factor improvement
figures.denominator_def: % change in annual approved new drugs per 10% improvement in the named factor

derivation: eps_C = 10 x c x tau x delta with c=0.30-0.40 (Phase III share of capitalised cost), tau=0.5-0.7 (time-proportional conduct cost at $55,716/day [E-3021]), delta=0.6; = 0.9 to 1.7. Add rescue of programs terminated for enrollment failure: probability of enrollment-driven program death rho=0.03-0.08, PoS_new/PoS_old ~ 1 + 0.1 x rho, contributing 0.3-0.8. Add a queueing multiplier of 1.3-1.6 because 48% of sites under-enrol or enrol nobody [E-3020] and >80% of trials miss the enrollment timeline. Total 1.5-4.0, point 2.5.

claim: B4 precision-medicine fragmentation elasticity is estimated at 0.5-2.5% per 10% reduction in screening burden, point 1.2%.
source_title: Agent C elasticity model

figures.unit: % change in annual approvals per 10% factor improvement
figures.denominator_def: % change in annual approved new drugs per 10% improvement in the named factor

derivation: Improvement defined as a 10% cut in samples screened per enrolled patient, holding enrichment constant. eps_C = 10 x c x tau x delta with c=0.15 (screening and prescreening share of trial cost in biomarker trials), tau=0.6, delta=0.6 = 0.5; plus schedule effect through B3 channel 0.3-2.0. Sign caution: reducing fragmentation itself (looser eligibility) would lower PoS via lost enrichment, so the elasticity is only positive when defined as screening efficiency.

claim: B5 regulatory review elasticity in the US is estimated at 0.1-1.0% per 10% improvement, point 0.4%.
source_title: Agent C elasticity model

figures.unit: % change in annual approvals per 10% factor improvement
figures.denominator_def: % change in annual approved new drugs per 10% improvement in the named factor

derivation: Review occupies roughly 10-12 months of a 9.1-year clinical development span [E-3004], so c is about 0.03 and tau about 0.5, giving eps_C = 10 x 0.03 x 0.5 x 0.6 = 0.09. Add up to 0.9 for evidence-standard effects (acceptance of NAM and biomarker evidence) which are more properly attributed to B2 and B15. FDA cleared 46-53 novel products in 2025 while meeting nearly all goal dates after losing 3,500 staff [E-3001, E-3029, E-3031], which is direct evidence of retained slack rather than binding queue.

claim: B6 manufacturing elasticity at whole-system level is 0.8-3.5% per 10% improvement, point 1.8%; for autologous cell therapy alone it is 15-40%, point 25%.
source_title: Agent C elasticity model

figures.unit: % change in annual approvals per 10% factor improvement
figures.denominator_def: % change in annual approved new drugs per 10% improvement in the named factor

derivation: System level: cell and gene therapy is roughly 10-15% of clinical programs. Within that segment eps is high because utilisation evidence is unambiguous (only 60% of candidates secured a slot [E-3038]; 25% manufacturing failure in NHL [E-3034]) - a 10% throughput gain converts near one-for-one into treated patients and into avoided program deaths, giving 15-40%. Weighting 0.125 x 25 = 3.1, discounted by 0.4-0.6 because much of the CGT gain accrues to commercial supply rather than to approvals, giving 1.3-1.9; band widened to 0.8-3.5 for ADC conjugation and fill-finish tightness [E-3039]. Offsetting evidence: viral vector suite capacity is modelled to exceed demand through 2031 [E-3036], so the AAV constraint is cost and yield per dose, not suite count.

claim: B7 delivery elasticity is estimated at 1-6% per 10% improvement, point 3%, with an explicitly wide band.
source_title: Agent C elasticity model

figures.unit: % change in annual approvals per 10% factor improvement
figures.denominator_def: % change in annual approved new drugs per 10% improvement in the named factor

derivation: Delivery acts by expanding the feasible target space rather than accelerating existing programs, so near-term eps_P is limited to programs already delivery-limited: f=0.15 of attrition, theta=0.10-0.40 gives 1.1 to 4.4. A long-run option-value term of up to 1.6 is added for indications currently outside the feasible set (CNS, solid tumour interior, muscle). The band is wide because no natural experiment relaxing delivery at scale has occurred; the ultrasound result [E-3043] is a 10-fold single-model gain, not a system observation.

claim: B8 toxicity and immunogenicity prediction elasticity is estimated at 3-9% per 10% improvement, point 6%.
source_title: Agent C elasticity model

figures.unit: % change in annual approvals per 10% factor improvement
figures.denominator_def: % change in annual approved new drugs per 10% improvement in the named factor

derivation: eps_P = 10 x 7.33 x f x theta with f=0.30 (toxicity share of failures [E-3045]) and theta=0.15-0.40; = 3.3 to 8.8. Toxicity failures are additionally concentrated late, so avoided spend adds a small capital channel; and toxicity drives about two thirds of post-launch withdrawals [E-3047], which raises expected commercial value per approval. Point 6.0.

claim: B9 wet-lab throughput elasticity is estimated at 0.3-2.0% per 10% improvement, point 0.9%; the IND-enabling toxicology sub-step alone is 1-4%.
source_title: Agent C elasticity model

figures.unit: % change in annual approvals per 10% factor improvement
figures.denominator_def: % change in annual approved new drugs per 10% improvement in the named factor

derivation: Discovery and preclinical wet work occupies a minority of capitalised cost, c=0.15-0.25, tau=0.4-0.6, delta=0.6, giving eps_C = 0.4 to 0.9. No queueing multiplier is applied to screening because automation evidence shows throughput already exceeding design capacity [E-3049] - the step is fast, not scarce. A multiplier of 2-4 is applied only to the NHP-dependent IND-enabling toxicology sub-step, where NPRCs cannot fill up to two thirds of requests [E-3050].

claim: B10 training-data scarcity elasticity is estimated at 0.3-2.5% per 10% improvement, point 1.0%.
source_title: Agent C elasticity model

figures.unit: % change in annual approvals per 10% factor improvement
figures.denominator_def: % change in annual approved new drugs per 10% improvement in the named factor

derivation: Data acts only through B1 and B8 model quality. A 10% increase in high-quality structure-plus-affinity data yields perhaps a 2-5% relative gain in predictive performance given log-scaling, and that gain passes into attrition at theta_2 = 0.1-0.3 of the B1/B8 elasticities. 0.03 x (10 + 6) = 0.5 at the low end; 0.05 x 0.3 x ... band widened to 0.3-2.5 to reflect that the PDBbind-class dataset is only ~7,000 complexes [E-3054] so proportional additions are cheap and large.

claim: B11 capital and reimbursement elasticity is estimated at 4-8% per 10% improvement, point 6%.
source_title: Agent C elasticity model

figures.unit: % change in annual approvals per 10% factor improvement
figures.denominator_def: % change in annual approved new drugs per 10% improvement in the named factor

derivation: This channel is close to linear: annual approvals Y = N x PoS and N is set by capital. A 10% increase in deployable capital (or equivalently 10% better capital efficiency) raises N by 10%, discounted by marginal-program quality delta=0.4-0.8, giving 4 to 8. Evidence that capital is currently binding rather than idle: early-stage rounds and dollars both fell in 2025 [E-3057, E-3058], ex-GLP-1 R&D return is 2.9% [E-3007] which is near or below cost of capital, and approved products have been withdrawn for commercial rather than technical reasons [E-3060]. Caveat: capital is an input rather than a process step, so a strict Theory-of-Constraints reading would ask what limits productive absorption of capital.

claim: B12 IP and freedom-to-operate elasticity is estimated at 0.05-1.0% per 10% improvement, point 0.3%.
source_title: Agent C elasticity model

figures.unit: % change in annual approvals per 10% factor improvement
figures.denominator_def: % change in annual approved new drugs per 10% improvement in the named factor

derivation: Patent pendency of 22.6 months to first action [E-3065] runs in parallel with, not in series with, clinical development, so it contributes no direct schedule delay. The channel is investment certainty: narrowed genus scope after Amgen v. Sanofi [E-3064] reduces expected exclusivity value and therefore feeds B11 at a small coefficient. eps = 0.1 x eps(B11) x 0.05-0.15 plus a term for AI-inventorship uncertainty, giving 0.05 to 1.0.

claim: B13 talent elasticity is estimated at 0.2-1.5% per 10% improvement, point 0.6%.
source_title: Agent C elasticity model

figures.unit: % change in annual approvals per 10% factor improvement
figures.denominator_def: % change in annual approved new drugs per 10% improvement in the named factor

derivation: Aggregate labour is in surplus: two employers alone shed about 22,500 roles [E-3068] while AI-specific postings grew 77% [E-3067]. A shortage confined to a narrow specialism with 4-6 month fill times [E-3066] cannot bind system output much, because the scarce specialists sit upstream of the abundant clinical capacity. eps_C = 10 x c x tau x delta with c=0.05 (AI/computational share of program cost), tau=0.4, delta=0.6 = 0.12; widened upward to 1.5 for organisational absorptive-capacity effects that are real but unquantified.

claim: B14 biosecurity and model regulation elasticity is estimated at 0.0-0.5% per 10% change, point 0.1%.
source_title: Agent C elasticity model

figures.unit: % change in annual approvals per 10% factor improvement
figures.denominator_def: % change in annual approved new drugs per 10% improvement in the named factor

derivation: No binding access regime exists today: the 2025 Executive Order deadlines had not produced revised frameworks as of July 2026 [E-3069], and only 3% of surveyed biological AI tools carry any safeguard [E-3070], with access ranging from restricted to open weights [E-3071]. With essentially no enforced constraint in place, relaxing it further cannot raise output; the elasticity is therefore near zero now and is properly a downside risk term rather than a lever.

claim: B15 endpoint and biomarker qualification elasticity is estimated at 1.5-5% per 10% improvement, point 3%.
source_title: Agent C elasticity model

figures.unit: % change in annual approvals per 10% factor improvement
figures.denominator_def: % change in annual approved new drugs per 10% improvement in the named factor

derivation: Two channels. Duration and size: absent a qualified surrogate, confirmatory trials must run to hard clinical outcomes, so c=0.30, tau=0.4, delta=0.6 gives eps_C = 0.7. Probability: better endpoints reduce false-negative Phase II readouts, f=0.10 of attrition with theta=0.2-0.4 gives 1.5 to 2.9. Constraint evidence is direct: only 11 biomarkers have ever been qualified, surrogate qualification plans take a median 47 months, and only 5 of 61 accepted projects were surrogates [E-3072, E-3073].

claim: B16 protocol complexity and operational data burden elasticity is estimated at 1.0-3.5% per 10% improvement, point 2.0%.
source_title: Agent C elasticity model

figures.unit: % change in annual approvals per 10% factor improvement
figures.denominator_def: % change in annual approved new drugs per 10% improvement in the named factor

derivation: eps_C = 10 x c x tau x delta with c=0.35 (Phase III share of capitalised cost), tau=0.35-0.55 (share of conduct cost driven by procedure count and data capture), delta=0.6 = 0.7 to 1.2, plus a schedule term because enrollment duration rose 36.9% over a decade [E-3077] alongside a 60% rise in procedures [E-3075]. Uniquely, the removable slack is documented: about a third of procedures do not serve primary or key secondary endpoints [E-3076], so theta is close to 1 for that fraction. Point 2.0.

claim: Elasticities across B1, B2, B8 and B10 are not additive because they act on overlapping attrition mass; the naive sum overstates joint effect by roughly a factor of 1.5-2.
source_title: Agent C elasticity model

figures.denominator_def: % change in annual approved new drugs per 10% improvement in the named factor

derivation: B1 (f=0.45 efficacy), B2 (f=0.25 model predictivity) and B8 (f=0.30 toxicity) together imply f_total = 1.00, i.e. the whole failure mass, while B10 acts only through B1 and B8. Simultaneous 10% improvement in all four therefore yields at most eps_joint = 10 x 7.33 x 1.00 x theta_eff, with theta_eff ~ 0.15-0.35, i.e. 11-26%, versus a naive sum of 21%. Report joint effects using the pooled formula, never the sum.

claim: Amdahl ceiling: eliminating discovery entirely removes at most about 30-40% of total elapsed development time and leaves cumulative PoS unchanged unless target and toxicity selection also improve.
source_title: Agent C elasticity model

figures.denominator_def: % change in annual approved new drugs per 10% improvement in the named factor

derivation: Total elapsed time = discovery (3-6 years, anchor under test) + clinical 9.1 years [E-3004] + review ~1 year [E-3029 context]. Discovery share = 3/(3+10.1) = 0.23 to 6/(6+10.1) = 0.37. Setting discovery to zero therefore caps time reduction at 23-37%. Because cumulative PoS from Phase I is 14.3% [E-3002] and is set by clinical attrition, discovery compression alone does not move it; the AI Phase I signal (21 of 24 [E-3008]) does not extend to Phase II.
